correctness.rationale: For the specified nearest-neighbor delayed Fisher–KPP lattice, the source supplies the linearly selected minimal speed as a positive double root of Delta_tau(c,lambda)=c lambda-d L(lambda)-exp(-c lambda tau). The proof reconstructs both double-root equations, establishes lambda_tau->0 and c_tau->0, and derives the exact identities E=d lambda^2(p-ell) and tau E=m/p-1. These imply y(p-ell)->1, z=log(tau)+o(1), y=log(tau)-1+o(1), and finally tau c_tau^2/d=log(tau)+1+o(1). The claim is limited to fixed d>0 and unit delayed-growth coefficient.

originality.rationale: The literature comparison found no statement of the additive-constant large-delay law for this exact lattice model in the accessible primary text and search results. The main primary source gives the double-root characterization but not this parameter asymptotic in the relevant sections read. A highly relevant 2006 lattice paper could not be obtained in full text and is retained as a residual risk; the abstract alone does not establish coverage. Search absence is not treated as a novelty proof.
residual_risks: The full text of Ma, Weng and Zou (2006) was not obtained. Its broad delayed-lattice scope makes it the principal unresolved originality risk, although the accessible abstract does not state the large-delay expansion.
The result is for fixed d>0 and normalized growth coefficient one; no claim is made for other reaction laws, nonlocal kernels, continuous diffusion, or added instantaneous mortality.
No independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The delay dependence of the minimal invasion speed is a natural quantitative question for delayed population-spread models. The asymptotic gives more than the order of decay: the additive constant +1 refines the scale and supplies a precise large-delay benchmark for the exact lattice dispersion relation. It is not presented as a general theorem for other models.
